title: Bolognese Ragu
subtitle: Slow-cooked meat sauce for pasta
excerpt: Good bolognese is not a quick tomato sauce -- it is a slow braise where the meat becomes tender and the sauce turns deep and coating. The milk goes in near the end and softens any sharpness from the tomatoes.
sourceNotes: The registered recipe for ragu alla bolognese, filed with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1982, contains no garlic, no herbs, and uses wine as its liquid. This version is a home-cook synthesis that keeps the long, slow cook and milk finish while using pantry staples.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch and freeze in labelled portions.

content.text: The soffritto (onion, carrot, and celery) needs a full 10 minutes over low heat before the meat goes in. If it colours too fast, add a splash of water and lower the heat.
Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over low heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Increase the heat to medium-high, add the beef mince and pork mince, and cook, breaking up the meat, until browned all over and any liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes, bay leaves, and thyme. Season well, then add 200 ml of water. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to very low, half-cover the pan, and cook for 90 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes and adding a splash of water if the sauce catches.
Stir in the milk and cook uncovered for a further 15 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove the bay leaves before serving.

items.symptom: Sauce catches and burns on the bottom.
items.cause: Heat too high or not enough liquid.
items.fix: Add 100 ml of water, stir well, and reduce the heat further. The sauce should barely blip at a simmer.

items.symptom: Watery sauce after a long cook.
items.cause: Lid not left uncovered enough to reduce, or too much water added.
items.fix: Remove the lid entirely for the last 20-30 minutes and increase heat slightly.
